title: Resample sensors to 15 minutes and flag frozen ones
prompt:
Write `resample_15min(df)`. `df` is a Polars DataFrame of one-minute readings with columns `ts` (datetime), `sensor` (str) and `temp` (float), in no particular order and with gaps.

Return one row per sensor per 15-minute window (windows start at :00, :15, :30 and :45) with columns `sensor`, `window` (the window's start), `mean_temp`, `n` (readings in the window) and `stuck`. `stuck` is true when a window has **at least 10 readings that are all identical**: a frozen sensor, not merely a quiet one. Sort by sensor, then window. Use Polars expressions, not Python loops.

`from data import readings` gives you the test data to try in Run.
hints: Polars has a time-based group-by: `group_by_dynamic("ts", every="15m", group_by="sensor")`, followed by `.agg(...)`. What does it need from the row order?

It needs rows sorted by time within each sensor: sort by sensor and ts first. In `.agg`, take `pl.col("temp").mean()`, `pl.len()` and `pl.col("temp").std()`; a frozen sensor has a standard deviation of exactly 0. Then build `stuck` with `with_columns`, rename `ts` to `window`, and select the five columns.

misconceptions.stuck-needs-evidence: Zero variance over a handful of readings isn't evidence of a frozen sensor; require enough readings in the window.
